MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a factor of 48? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 7
   C. 5
   D. 9

2. What number is the Roman numeral VII? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 7
   C. 3
   D. 1

3. What number is the Roman numeral VIII? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 1
   C. 3
   D. 2

4. Estimate 5,382 + 3,617 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 9,000
   B. 9,099
   C. 9,010
   D. 8,990

5. Work out 2,345 + 1,432. (1 mark)
   A. 3,787
   B. 3,777
   C. 3,677
   D. 4,777

6. Work out 4,236 + 1,528. (1 mark)
   A. 5,774
   B. 5,754
   C. 5,664
   D. 5,764

7. Work out 8,500 − 3,275. (1 mark)
   A. 5,235
   B. 5,375
   C. 5,225
   D. 5,125

8. Work out 5,008 − 2,999. (1 mark)
   A. 2,019
   B. 1,909
   C. 2,009
   D. 3,991

9. What is 36 × 40? (1 mark)
   A. 144
   B. 1,440
   C. 76
   D. 14,400

10. What is the next number in the pattern 3, 6, 12, 24, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 30
   B. 27
   C. 36
   D. 48

11. What is 48 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 48,000
   B. 480
   C. 148
   D. 4,800

12. What is 84 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 22
   B. 31
   C. 21
   D. 20

13. What is 72 ÷ 3? (1 mark)
   A. 25
   B. 23
   C. 34
   D. 24

14. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 6 × 7 = 42? (1 mark)
   A. 42 ÷ 6 = 7
   B. 42 ÷ 6 = 6
   C. 42 ÷ 42 = 6
   D. 7 ÷ 6 = 42

15. Ali writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 7/4
   B. 3/8
   C. 11/5
   D. 1 3/4

16. A circle is cut into 5 equal parts and 2 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 3/2
   B. 5/3
   C. 2/5
   D. 3/5

17. What is 4/9 of 27? (1 mark)
   A. 15
   B. 3
   C. 12
   D. 13

18. In the number 13.42, the digit 4 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Hundredths
   C. Tenths
   D. Tens

19. Write 45/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.54
   B. 0.045
   C. 4.5
   D. 0.45

20. In the number 8.30, the digit 3 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tenths
   B. Tens
   C. Hundredths
   D. Ones

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how multiplication can be used to check that 72 ÷ 6 = 12. (3 marks)

22. A tanker fills 100 jerrycans of 20 litres each. How many litres is that? (2 marks)

23. For the number 4,835: (a) write it in expanded form, (b) give the total value of the digit 8, (c) round it to the nearest ten, (d) say whether it is even or odd. (5 marks)

24. Add 4,236 and 1,528. Show your working. (3 marks)

25. Write 4 3/8 as an improper fraction. (3 marks)

26. Find the first common multiple of 4 and 6 by writing the first six multiples of each number. (4 marks)

27. Estimate 7,483 − 2,196 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact answer. (4 marks)

28. On a poultry farm each of 16 hens lays 21 eggs in one month. How many eggs are laid altogether? (3 marks)

29. Add 3,568 and 2,276 and say how many times you regrouped. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 12
   48 ÷ 12 = 4 with nothing left over, so 12 is a factor of 48. The others leave a remainder.

2. B — 7
   VII stands for 7.

3. A — 8
   VIII stands for 8.

4. A — 9,000
   5,382 rounds to 5,380 and 3,617 rounds to 3,620. 5,380 + 3,620 = 9,000.

5. B — 3,777
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 2,345 + 1,432 = 3,777.

6. D — 5,764
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 4,236 + 1,528 = 5,764.

7. C — 5,225
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225. Check: 5,225 + 3,275 = 8,500.

8. C — 2,009
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 5,008 − 2,999 = 2,009. Check: 2,009 + 2,999 = 5,008.

9. B — 1,440
   36 × 4 = 144, then × 10 gives 1,440.

10. D — 48
   The rule is multiply by 2. 24 × 2 = 48.

11. D — 4,800
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 48 × 100 = 4,800.

12. C — 21
   4 × 21 = 84, so 84 ÷ 4 = 21.

13. D — 24
   3 × 24 = 72, so 72 ÷ 3 = 24.

14. A — 42 ÷ 6 = 7
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 6 × 7 = 42, we know 42 ÷ 6 = 7 and 42 ÷ 7 = 6.

15. B — 3/8
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 3/8 is less than one whole.

16. D — 3/5
   Not shaded: 5 − 2 = 3 parts, so 3/5.

17. C — 12
   27 ÷ 9 = 3 and 3 × 4 = 12. So 4/9 of 27 is 12.

18. C — Tenths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 13.42 the digit 4 is in the tenths place.

19. D — 0.45
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 45/100 = 0.45.

20. A — Tenths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 8.30 the digit 3 is in the tenths place.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Multiply the answer by the divisor: 12 × 6 = 72. This gives the starting number, so the division is correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for multiplying the answer by the divisor, 1 mark for 12 × 6 = 72, 1 mark for the conclusion.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2,000 litres
   Working / marking points: 20 × 100 = 2,000. 1 mark for the multiplication and 1 mark for units.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 4,000 + 800 + 30 + 5 (b) 800 (c) 4,840 (d) odd because it ends in 5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part; part (a) needs all four addends, part (b) 8 × 100, part (c) the ones digit 5 rounds up, part (d) needs the reason from the ones digit (1 mark for the classification plus reason together).

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: 5,764
   Working / marking points: Ones 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 carry 1 (1 mark); tens 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 (1 mark); hundreds 2 + 5 = 7, thousands 4 + 1 = 5, answer 5,764 (1 mark).

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 35/8
   Working / marking points: 4 × 8 = 32 (1 mark); 32 + 3 = 35 (1 mark); denominator stays 8 (1 mark).

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. The first common multiple is 12.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct list and 2 marks for identifying 12.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 7,480 − 2,200 = 5,280. Exact: 5,287.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for 5,280, 1 mark for 5,287.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 336 eggs
   Working / marking points: 21 × 6 = 126 (1 mark); 21 × 10 = 210 (1 mark); 126 + 210 = 336 (1 mark).

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 5,844. You regrouped twice (ones to tens, tens to hundreds).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct sum, 1 mark for the carries, 1 mark for saying twice.
